ArXiv cs.AI.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25043v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. ArXiv cs.AI.title: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25070v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven framework, CodeReAct agent, designed to enhance industrial equipment maintenance through natural language (NL) interactions. The framework employs an advanced AI agentic approach to interpret human instructions, providing knowledge extraction, asset status summarization, and work order recommendations. It identifies patterns and trends and predicts work orders by standardizing industrial data into business objects (BOs) and utilizing analytical function API calls. The AI agent operates through a Thought-Action-Ob

ArXiv cs.AI.title: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25087v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present SailSearch, a human-guided workflow for algorithmic research with two language-model agents, and report results on Market Split and maximum independent set (MIS). For Market Split, our randomized algorithm searches across multiple lattice bases, dividing computation between enumeration and continued basis reduction. ArXiv cs.AI.title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). In practice, designing, training, and evaluating complex models demands modifying multi-file repositories to reproduce results, debug training runs, integrate datasets, and port frameworks. However, existing MLE benchmarks limit agents to single-file edits without full repository or shell access, and common repository-level software engineering benchmarks have rapidly saturated. ArXiv cs.AI.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' grad

ArXiv cs.AI.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25111v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Data science workflows often require tools that presume non-trivial technical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) reduce this barrier, but a gap remains between flexible general-purpose agents and statistically controlled pipelines. We introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data-agent platform that combines reusable, LLM-selected skills with deterministic diagnostic guardrails. Skills provide extensible task knowledge. Symbolic validation can accept a proposed method, request clarification or replanning, override an unsuitable me

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25135v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). ArXiv cs.AI.title: EverydayBench: Evaluating Satisfactory Completion of Live User-Facing Digital Work
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25146v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Everyday digital tasks, from selecting products and planning trips to conducting research and creating artifacts, require AI agents to deliver useful outcomes rather than merely retrieve web information. Yet evaluating these outcomes on the live web is challenging, as a single request may admit multiple valid results, and changing web information can alter which results remain valid over time. ArXiv cs.AI.title: A Verifier from the Past: Test-Time Compute for Time Series Foundation Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25171v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language models by spending additional inference compute to generate, verify, and select among candidate outputs, but this recipe has not transferred directly to time series forecasting. A language model can verify a proof or vote across samples, but a forecaster must be causal; it cannot use future information to score a candidate. ArXiv cs.AI.title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25184v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Empirical finance research often reuses natural experiments to study other outcomes, raising concerns about multiple testing and publication bias. We use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments. The agents rebuild the data, reproduce each paper's main estimate and re-estimate it across grids totaling 62,409 estimated defensible specifications. ArXiv cs.AI.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25198v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Every empirical analysis on observational data rests on dozens of defensible analytical choices ("forks") that its readers cannot see. We develop an agentic multiverse analysis (AMA) framework that makes a conclusion's sensitivity to those choices visible at scale, and we position it as a decision-support instrument for human experts. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25214v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scientific discovery requires revisiting the hypotheses in light of new evidence and identifying promising directions beyond those already explored. However, research agents often make claims that are not supported by their observations, explore a narrow hypothesis space, and retain beliefs despite recognizing conflicting evidence. These failures motivate the search for an explicit epistemic state that captures both beliefs about existing hypotheses and directions for further exploration. ArXiv cs.AI.title: MKA: Evaluating Multimodal Knowledge Agents on end-to-end professional tasks
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25228v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, which measures how well autonomous agents perform end-to-end professional knowledge work that depends on visual understanding. Each task requires an agent to extract and combine information from multiple visually dense files, such as CAD blueprints, electronics schematics, radiographs, complex charts and geospatial maps, and to produce a standalone deliverable in .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, .docx, .html or .png format. ArXiv cs.AI.title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.25236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unplanned 30-day readmissions among patients with diabetes mellitus impose a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet most predictive models use only structured electronic health record (EHR) data and ignore free-text clinical notes, which often contain code-mixed Hindi-English (Hinglish) phrasing and negation that general-purpose language models parse unreliably. Wired — Business.title: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’
Wired — Business.description: Henrijs Dandzbergs dropped out of high school to join startup accelerator Y Combinator. With a new breed of missile, he wants to make killing as efficient as possible for the US and its military allies.

Wired — Business.title: What’s With All These Outages?
Wired — Business.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss the outages that have swept digital life over the past week, where new money from Anthropic’s IPO is going, and the AI chip world post-Jensen Huang.

Wired — Business.title: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
Wired — Business.description: In Taiwan, some food vendors are distancing themselves from Nvidia’s former CEO. Others stand by him. “It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire,” says one shop owner.

Wired — Business.title: Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Highlights the AI Giant’s Worst Enemy—Itself
Wired — Business.description: Investors betting a barnstorming $107 billion will weigh whether the company’s AI safety strategy and growing public anger toward data centers could impact its growth.

Wired — Business.title: Gig Work Is Invading Nursing Homes. The Risks Can Be Deadly
Wired — Business.description: Inspection reports detailing elder care facilities show that little to no worker onboarding can lead to dangerous mistakes and overwhelmed nurses, a WIRED and Proof News investigation has found.

Wired — Business.title: Does Nvidia Got This? Interim CEO Colette Kress Says It’s Got This
Wired — Business.description: WIRED is tallying up how many times Nvidia’s interim CEO has assured everyone that the company has everything under control.

Wired — Business.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
Wired — Business.description: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.

Wired — Business.title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity
Wired — Business.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress sought to ease employee concerns following Jensen Huang’s ouster, in part by promising to increase compensation.

Wired — Business.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
Wired — Business.description: Thomas Nagel has done landmark work on consciousness in nonhumans; this week, he won the million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his contributions to the field. And he has a lot of thoughts on AI.

Wired — Business.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
Wired — Business.description: Despite pressure from President Trump, Elon Musk, and Silicon Valley executives, Nvidia’s board says it “does not intend” to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO.

Wired — Business.title: Jensen Huang Says He’s Open to Coming Back to Nvidia
Wired — Business.description: Huang said in a statement that he “would be honored” to return as Nvidia CEO if the board of directors supported the decision.

Wired — Business.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
Wired — Business.description: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.

Wired — Business.title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business
Wired — Business.description: Google and Apple alumni Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes are applying what they learned running software companies and designing iPhones to manufacturing lethal munitions.

Wired — Business.title: Jensen Huang Is Gone. Now What?
Wired — Business.description: After a shocking downfall, Nvidia’s CEO is out of a job. WIRED’s Lauren Goode explains what that means for the world’s most critical chip company, the AI industry, and Jensen Huang himself.

Wired — Business.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
Wired — Business.description: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.
